Reassembles newline-delimited records from arbitrary network chunks.

Upstream proxies split event streams at arbitrary byte boundaries, so a record may
arrive across several reads. The buffer keeps the trailing partial line until its newline
arrives. Bytes are decoded only after a full line is available, because a multi-byte
UTF-8 character can be split between chunks. A final line with no newline is not
returned until flush is called.

Ordered batch writer for inventory updates.

Each batch is written in a single transaction and batches are committed
strictly in submission order. A failed batch is retried in place, so later
batches wait behind it; there is no skip-ahead.

Pull the next batch of items from an iterator and return them as a list.

The iterator is consumed in place, so calling this repeatedly walks through the
stream. The final batch may be shorter than size, and an exhausted iterator
yields an empty list.

Advance tokens past the first occurrence of marker.

The marker itself is consumed and not returned. If it never appears, the
iterator is fully exhausted and False is returned.

Transaction boundary used by the request middleware.

Handlers originally committed by hand, and a forgotten commit silently
discarded writes when the pooled connection was recycled. The middleware
now opens one scope per request and commits when the handler returns
normally. Any exception, including ones the handler later converts to an
error response, triggers a rollback first. Savepoints are intentionally
unsupported, so partial failures inside a handler must be handled before
the scope exits.

Frame codec: 4-byte big-endian length, then payload.

read_frame returns None only on a clean end of stream at a frame boundary; a stream
cut mid-frame raises EOFError instead.

Length-prefixed framing with a CRC32 trailer.

Every frame ends with a 4-byte CRC32 of the payload only; the length prefix is not
covered. A corrupted length therefore surfaces as a checksum failure on whatever bytes
happen to follow, not as a distinct error. After a ChecksumError the stream position is
undefined, so callers should close the connection instead of trying to resynchronize.

Insert a note and its tags atomically, returning the new note id.

The write lock is taken up front with BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Under the default deferred BEGIN,
two concurrent CLI invocations could both read and then fail while upgrading to a write,
and SQLite reports "database is locked" at once instead of waiting for busy_timeout.
This replaced the retry loops the importers used to wrap around the insert. The
connection must not already be inside a transaction, or BEGIN raises OperationalError.

Call work(cursor) and commit, returning its result.

Any exception rolls back everything work did and propagates unchanged. work must not call commit() or rollback() on the connection: either one ends the transaction early, so a later failure would undo only the statements after that point.

Remove duplicate events from a list.

Returns a new list containing the first occurrence of each event id.

Keep the last event for each payload, in order of first appearance.

Unlike id-based deduplication, a later duplicate replaces the earlier one's data
but not its position. Payloads must be JSON-serializable; otherwise TypeError
is raised partway through and no result is returned.

Lowercases the whole address, including the local part.

This deviates from RFC 5321, which allows case-sensitive local parts, but
the upstream CRM treats them as case-insensitive. Invalid input yields None
rather than raising, so callers must filter the results.

Masks email addresses before records leave the pipeline for analytics.

Only the first character of the local part survives, and the domain is kept
so that provider-level statistics still work. Addresses without an "@" are
replaced entirely with a fixed placeholder instead of being passed through,
which avoids leaking free-text values that landed in the email column by
mistake.
A clock whose time only changes when advance() is called.

Wraps a real time source and shifts every reading by a fixed offset.

The offset is applied to the value returned, not to the underlying source,
so several OffsetClock instances sharing one source do not affect each
other. Sleeping is never faked: sleep_until() still blocks for real time,
which keeps timeout tests honest but makes them slow.
Replace secret query parameter values in a URL with asterisks.
Drops webhook events whose id has already been seen recently.

Suppresses repeated payment notifications.

The provider retries a delivery until it receives a 2xx, so the same event
can arrive several times, sometimes seconds apart. Ids are remembered in a
bounded set backed by a deque that records first-seen order. Once the limit
is reached the oldest id is evicted, so a retry arriving after that many
newer events is treated as new. Handlers must stay idempotent regardless.

Timeout wrapper for pipeline stages.

CancelledError is re-raised, never swallowed, so callers can tell a
timeout from a stage failure.

Fan-out helpers where one failing branch cancels its siblings.

Uses asyncio.TaskGroup, so Python 3.11 or newer is required. Failures
arrive wrapped in an ExceptionGroup; catch them with except*, because a
plain except Exception will not match the inner errors by type.

# Earlier releases truncated the index in place, and an interrupted run left
# an empty file that the next invocation treated as "no entries". Writing a
# sibling temp file and renaming it over the original means readers see either
# the old index or the new one. The sibling must share the target's
# filesystem, which is why mkstemp gets dir= instead of the default /tmp.

# The length prefix is little-endian because the first embedded clients
# were ARM boards that wrote it with a raw memcpy, and the gateway kept
# the format when it moved to Python. Every other integer is big-endian.
Computes exponential retry delays with jitter for pipeline stages.

Retry schedule used by the warehouse loader when the upstream API throttles.

Each delay is drawn between the base and three times the previous delay,
then clamped to the cap. This replaced a fixed doubling schedule after
parallel workers kept retrying in lockstep and re-triggering the rate
limiter. The instance stores the previous delay, so share one instance
per worker, never across threads.

Guard against a regression where float inputs were rounded wrongly.

The payout job once passed floats straight to Decimal, so 2.675 became
2.67499999... and rounded down. Values must be converted via str first,
which gives the expected 2.68.
# Keep the lock held through the read and the write; the worker pool shares this instance.

Parse CSV text into dictionaries and push each row onto a queue.

Parse an uploaded CSV blob using a semicolon delimiter by default.

Early uploads came from a spreadsheet export used by the regional offices,
which writes semicolons because of their locale settings, so the worker
defaults to that rather than a comma. The bytes are decoded as utf-8-sig to
drop the byte order mark that export adds. Rows are returned as lists, and
blank lines are discarded rather than yielding empty rows.

Make devtools.clock.now() return moment inside the with block.

Patches the name where it is looked up, not datetime itself, because
the built-in datetime class cannot be patched directly. Naive moments
are rejected with ValueError.

Regression: an event just before midnight UTC must land in the earlier day's partition.

The old implementation read the clock twice, once for the date and once for the hour, so a tick between the calls could pair a new date with a stale hour. The clock is now read once per call.
Helpers for running and cleaning up subprocesses in a data pipeline.

Launch pipeline helpers in their own process group and tear them down.

Shell wrappers used by the ingest stage spawn grandchildren, and killing
only the direct child left those running after the stage failed, holding
file locks on the staging directory. Children are therefore started with
start_new_session=True and cleanup signals the whole group with SIGTERM,
escalating to SIGKILL after a grace period. POSIX only: os.killpg does not
exist on Windows.

Subprocess cleanup for pipeline stages.

terminate_all() is safe to call more than once and ignores processes that
have already exited. It must be called from the parent process only;
forked workers inherit the registry but cannot wait on siblings' children.

Applies queued row updates in the order they were enqueued.

Updates for the same row id must never be reordered, so the worker uses a
single consumer thread and a FIFO queue.

Sequence-numbered update buffer for the sync worker.

Updates may arrive out of order from the network. They are held until every
lower sequence number has been applied, so a gap blocks all later updates
indefinitely; callers needing a timeout must drop the buffer themselves.

Last-writer-wins coalescing of profile updates.

Within one flush window only the newest update per user survives, but
users are still flushed in the order of their first update. This keeps
downstream audit logs stable. Relies on dict preserving insertion order,
which is why the pending map is never rebuilt, only mutated. The earlier
version sorted by timestamp and produced audit entries that disagreed with
the upstream event log when clocks skewed between producers.

Pull the next batch of items from an iterator and return them as a list.

The iterator is consumed in place, so calling this repeatedly walks through the
stream. The final batch may be shorter than size, and an exhausted iterator
yields an empty list.

Count lines containing needle, exhausting the iterable as a side effect.

The helper was written for file handles streamed from large build logs, where
materializing a list was too costly. A generator passed here cannot be reused
afterwards; wrap it with itertools.tee first if a second pass is needed.

Advance tokens past the first occurrence of marker.

The marker itself is consumed and not returned. If it never appears, the

Regression test for duplicate customers from the legacy export.

The same person appeared twice, once with a precomposed accent and once
with a decomposed one. Both spellings must normalize to one string; the
pipeline used to compare raw strings and kept both rows, inflating counts.

Regression test: composed and decomposed forms of the same id must normalize identically.

Previously, ids typed on different platforms produced two separate queue entries
for what was logically the same job.

Handlers originally committed by hand, and a forgotten commit silently

now opens one scope per request and commits when the handler returns
normally. Any exception, including ones the handler later converts to an
error response, triggers a rollback first. Savepoints are intentionally

Binary framing helpers for the sync command.

Reads and writes length-prefixed frames on a stream.

Thread helpers for the batch-rename command.

Workers take paths from a shared queue and append results under a lock.

Progress tracking shared by the download threads and the status line.

Early releases let every worker print its own progress, which interleaved
output on narrow terminals. Workers now only bump a counter guarded by a
Condition, and the main thread is the sole writer to stderr. render() blocks
on the condition and wakes on every increment, so it redraws once per
completed download.

Lock order is cache_lock, then log_lock, everywhere in this module.

Taking them in the reverse order from a new helper will deadlock against
store() and flush(), and nothing here detects it. File writes happen after
both locks are released.
Signs outbound webhook requests for the delivery worker using HMAC-SHA256.
Request signing for the sync worker. Signatures cover the path only, not the query string, so parameters must never carry authority.

Signing for requests issued from retry loops.

A fresh timestamp is generated on every call, so a retried request must be
re-signed rather than replaying the headers from the first attempt; the
server rejects signatures older than 60 seconds.

# The insert and delete must share one transaction. The archive job
# originally committed between them, and a crash in that window left
# rows in both tables, which double-counted them in the daily rollup.

Filter out events whose id is already in seen_ids, mutating seen_ids in place.

Ids of kept events are added to the set, so calling this twice with the same
set and the same batch returns an empty list the second time.

Regression test for the nightly batch that double-processed records near midnight.

Timestamps one second apart across 00:00 UTC must land in different batch days, regardless of the host's local timezone, because the worker previously called datetime.fromtimestamp without a tz argument.

# The legacy log scrubber matches on the first and last character of the local
# part, which is why those two survive masking; the log format predates this helper.

Retrying UDP sender for pipeline heartbeats.

Sockets returned here are non-blocking-safe only for sends. Waiting for an
acknowledgement uses a one second timeout, and a missed acknowledgement is
reported as False rather than raised, because heartbeats are best effort.
Any other socket error still propagates to the caller.

Email address normalization helpers for the ingest pipeline.

Provides functions to clean, validate, and deduplicate email addresses
read from CSV exports before they are loaded into the warehouse.

Email canonicalization used when joining contact records across sources.

The marketing export and the billing database were historically keyed on
different forms of the same address, which produced duplicate customers. To
fix this, the join key strips "+tag" suffixes from the local part and
removes dots for gmail.com addresses only. The canonical form is meant for
matching and must never be written back as the contact's display address.
The domain is always lowercased via an IDNA-aware step in the loader.
A clock whose time only changes when advance() is called.

Returns a fixed timestamp and refuses to move backwards.

Tests that need time to pass should call tick(); set() raises ValueError
for earlier values, because the reminder scheduler assumes monotonic time.

Replacement for the system clock injected into the deadline checker.

The checker used to call datetime.now() directly, which made overdue tests
depend on wall time and fail around midnight. It now takes a clock object,
and this stub stores a list of timestamps that are handed out one per call
to now(). Running out of values raises IndexError on purpose, so a test
that reads the clock more often than expected fails loudly.

Write an uploaded stream to a temp file and return its path.

The file is removed if reading the stream fails.

Remove a per-request scratch directory after the response is sent.

Request handlers used to rely on the framework's teardown hook, but it does
not run when a client disconnects mid-stream, which left scratch trees
piling up. Handlers now call this from a finally block. The path must be
inside root; anything else raises ValueError so a bad request id can never
point the cleanup at an unrelated directory.

Render rows into a temporary file and return an open handle positioned at the start.

The file is created with delete=True, so it disappears as soon as the caller
closes the handle. Callers must not reopen it by name: on Windows that fails
while the handle is open. Intended to be passed straight to the response streamer.
Replace secret query parameter values in a URL with asterisks.

Mask secret values in parsed JSON before it reaches the audit log.

Walks dicts and lists recursively instead of regex-scrubbing the raw text,
which an earlier version did and which missed values containing escaped
quotes. Returns a new structure; the input is left untouched.

Remove user:password@ from a URL's authority.

The port is preserved. IPv6 literals lose their brackets, so do not use
this on them. The hostname is also lowercased as a side effect of urlsplit.
Drops webhook events whose id has already been seen recently.

Regression: peeking at the first record to read the schema used to
drop it from the output, because next() advanced the shared iterator.
The helper now chains the peeked record back in front of the remainder,
so downstream stages receive the complete stream in original order.

# The registry's rate-limit window outlasts our 1/2/4 second schedule, and a fixed
# schedule once got CI tokens throttled, so a 429 carrying Retry-After sleeps for
# that many seconds instead. Only the integer form is handled; an HTTP-date value
# raises ValueError here and ends the retries.

Environment parsing for the backup command-line tool.

Reads settings from os.environ and returns a typed Settings object.

Settings are read from the environment once, through an injectable mapping.

The original version called os.getenv inside each command handler, which made
the tests depend on process-global state and leak values between cases. Passing
the mapping explicitly lets tests supply a plain dict. Empty strings are
treated as unset so that a shell export such as BACKUP_TARGET= falls back to
the default instead of producing an empty path.

Async worker pool that drains a queue of pipeline tasks.

Workers stop when cancelled and leave unfinished items in the queue.

Timeout wrapper for pipeline stages.

CancelledError is re-raised, never swallowed, so callers can tell a
timeout from a stage failure.

Graceful shutdown helpers for the ingest pipeline.

These were added after a deploy left half-written batch files on disk:
the old code cancelled tasks and exited without waiting for them to
unwind. Each stage is now shielded while it commits its batch, so a
cancellation request is delivered only after the commit finishes. The
scheduler in the orchestrator calls shutdown() on SIGTERM and expects
it to return once every stage has stopped.

This test makes sure the uploader retries after a transient 5xx from the
storage backend instead of raising right away. We mock the client to fail
once with a 503 and then succeed, and assert upload() is called twice and
returns normally. Added after INFRA-771 where a single blip failed an entire
nightly batch.

Verifies the lock is released even if the callback passed to with_lock
raises an exception. Without this the lock would stay held forever and
every subsequent caller would hang, which is exactly the deadlock this
test is guarding against. We patch the lock object and assert release()
is called in a finally-style path.

Confirms that when a batch insert has one bad row among many, the good
rows still get committed rather than the whole batch rolling back. This
matters because the caller reports per-row errors back to the user and
expects the successful rows to already be saved; an all-or-nothing rollback
would silently discard work the user believes succeeded.

reporting it, the route's one-line rejection would become the only record

The provider retries a delivery until it receives a 2xx, so the same event
can arrive several times, sometimes seconds apart. Ids are remembered in a
bounded set backed by a deque that records first-seen order. Once the limit
is reached the oldest id is evicted, so a retry arriving after that many
newer events is treated as new. Handlers must stay idempotent regardless.

Figures out whether a given logging call would actually render stack
frames if it ran.

The presence of exc_info isn't the whole question: the logging module
treats a falsy exc_info as absent, so exception(..., exc_info=None) prints
no traceback even though the keyword is there, while a bare exception(...)
does print one because the method defaults exc_info to True. We walk the
AST node, look at its keywords, and decide based on that.

Transaction boundary used by the request middleware.

Handlers originally committed by hand, and a forgotten commit silently
discarded writes when the pooled connection was recycled. The middleware
now opens one scope per request and commits when the handler returns
normally. Any exception, including ones the handler later converts to an
error response, triggers a rollback first. Savepoints are intentionally
unsupported, so partial failures inside a handler must be handled before
the scope exits.

connection must not already be inside a transaction, or BEGIN raises OperationalError.

Figures out whether a given logging call would actually render stack

Figures out whether a given logging call would actually render stack
frames if it ran.

The presence of exc_info isn't the whole question: the logging module
treats a falsy exc_info as absent, so exception(..., exc_info=None) prints
no traceback even though the keyword is there, while a bare exception(...)
does print one because the method defaults exc_info to True. We walk the
AST node, look at its keywords, and decide based on that.
